h: Clocks, Canals and the River Dee
p: Chester Gates sits on the northern side of the city near the M56, which makes it handy for families travelling from Manchester, Liverpool and the Wirral. It also puts you very close to Ellesmere Port, where there are a few more family favourites.

Cheshire Oaks Designer Outlet is just up the road, with dozens of shops and places to eat. Right next to it, Blue Planet Aquarium has sharks, rays and an underwater tunnel that kids love. If you like boats, the National Waterways Museum at Ellesmere Port is a fascinating collection of canal boats and old dockside buildings, where you can learn how goods once moved around the country.

Back in the city, the Eastgate Clock on the city walls is one of the most photographed clocks in the country, built to celebrate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee. It's a lovely spot for a family photo.

Down by the river, the Groves is a pretty riverside promenade where you can take a boat trip along the Dee, feed the ducks or grab an ice cream. Grosvenor Park, nearby, is a well-kept Victorian park with a miniature railway that's often running in the warmer months, and the Roman Amphitheatre sits just beside it.
Chester's centre is compact but busy, and parking can be pricey, so the park and ride sites are worth considering if you're heading in after your session.
With trampolines in the morning and Roman ruins in the afternoon, this is one of those places where a whole day just disappears.
